key_insight: Reference-free physics-informed neural networks resolve strong kinetic shocks accurately, but higher-order moments expose errors that bulk flow fields can conceal.
engineering_relevance: The approach could support predictive modeling of highly nonequilibrium shock flows where heat flux, stress and distribution-level accuracy matter.
method: Correct a mixture of end-state Maxwellians with a signed, unbounded neural factor and exact inflow conditions.
Minimize kinetic residuals in three norms plus conservation terms using Adam, self-scaled quasi-Newton optimization and Mach-number continuation.
Evaluate eight macroscopic and higher-order fields across BGK, Shakhov, nitrogen Rykov-type and hard-sphere Boltzmann models.
evidence_signal: After reference-free testing, the largest relative L2 difference from DSMC across eight hard-sphere Boltzmann fields was 0.19% at Mach 8 and 0.34% at Mach 10, with distribution agreement spanning six decades in velocity space.
watch_item: High-Mach BGK fourth-order moments required increased weighting of a passive reduced distribution and longer optimization; errors remained up to 7.1% at Mach 100.
paper_title: Physics-informed neural networks for strong normal shocks in kinetic relaxation models and the hard-sphere Boltzmann equation
